leftEvidence.title: Moses promises a prophet Israel must hear

points.label: Event action and claim
points.left: Moses says the LORD will raise a prophet like him from among Israel.
points.right: After six days Jesus takes three disciples up a high mountain; his face shines, his clothes become white, and Moses and Elijah appear speaking with him.

points.label: Response and consequence
points.left: God will put words in the prophet’s mouth and hold accountable anyone who refuses to listen.
points.right: Peter proposes three tents; a bright cloud overshadows them, the voice names the beloved Son and commands listening, and the frightened disciples finally see Jesus alone.

payload.posture: Deuteronomy commands Israel to listen to the prophet God will raise; Matthew’s voice commands the disciples to listen to Jesus.

rightEvidence.title: Jesus is transfigured before Peter, James, and John

payload.tension: Matthew does not quote the full Deuteronomy passage or erase its original covenant setting.
payload.title: The promised prophet and “listen to him”
